Enrollment URL and one-time token come w: Enrollment URL and one-time token come with the factory image or from the fleet manager. After the first successful contact the device holds its own certificate; the token is used up.
Shown in the fleet management next to th: Shown in the fleet management next to this installation, e.g. "Womo Mercedes KA-1525" (max. 200 characters)
Service staff of the fleet management ca: Service staff of the fleet management can open admin or vis-2 of this system from afar, without ioBroker.pro and without open ports: on request, this adapter connects to the fleet server for the duration of the access. Every access is logged with person and purpose, and is shown below while it lasts. Changing these settings ends running accesses. The console is off until you allow it here.
admin means full access to the system: admin means full access to the system
vis-2 shows the values of this system, e: vis-2 shows the values of this system, e.g. consumption
Allow the console (a shell on this syste: Allow the console (a shell on this system)
Only Linux. The shell runs as the user o: Only Linux. The shell runs as the user of ioBroker: full access to ioBroker, its data and, depending on the setup, to the system
Allow ETS to reach the KNX gateway: Allow ETS to reach the KNX gateway
Service staff can program the KNX instal: Service staff can program the KNX installation with ETS from afar, through the program bee-knx on their PC. To the gateway below, and to further gateways named in the fleet management if they are in the allowed network (see devices in the network below).
IP address or host name, with :port if n: IP address or host name, with :port if not 3671. Empty: as set in the adapter knx or openknx
Allow devices in the network to be reach: Allow devices in the network to be reached
Service staff can program a device in th: Service staff can program a device in this network with its own tool from afar, e.g. a LOGO! with LOGO!Soft Comfort or an S7 with TIA Portal, through the program bee-knx on their PC. Which devices, the fleet management says; only inside the networks and ports below, never this device itself.
Networks or single addresses, separated: Networks or single addresses, separated by commas; only private ones (10.x, 172.16-31.x, 192.168.x). Empty: the own subnets of this device. Also applies to further KNX gateways.
Separated by commas. Empty: any port. LO: Separated by commas. Empty: any port. LOGO! 8: 102 and 10005, S7: 102
Each line is a device in this network wh: Each line is a device in this network whose web interface service staff may open in the browser from the fleet management, by its name, e.g. a router, an inverter or a camera. Address as IP:port, e.g. 192.168.0.1 or 192.168.0.20:8080 (without port: 80), with https:// for HTTPS (port 443 is HTTPS anyway); a host name of this network works too. Only private addresses (10.x, 172.16-31.x, 192.168.x) or this system itself (127.0.0.1). The fleet management sees name and address; the device asks for its own login. An empty table offers nothing.

Updates only run inside the maintenance: Updates only run inside the maintenance window and when all conditions are met (e.g. installation not in use, battery charged, no roaming, vehicle standing).
Label: Label
Each line watches a state. Once its cond: Each line watches a state. Once its condition holds for longer than the delay, the fleet management shows a deviation with this severity and notifies by mail or Telegram as set there; once the condition is gone for as long, the deviation ends. Example: victron.0.voltage, "<", 11.5, Warning. "No update for (min)" reports a state that stopped changing, e.g. because its adapter hangs.
